reviewer.method: Independent round-2 pass over output/preview.mp4 after the author's targeted fix for the sole blocking issue raised in review/findings-preview-v11.json: shot-0's metronome arm (project.json shots[0], layer id prop-2) ticking ~10.7x faster than shots[1]/[2]'s rate, with no motivating event at the 2.358s internal cut. Did not trust the author's description of the fix; re-derived everything from the current files. Confirmed output/preview-reference/evidence.json's output_sha256 (590a2fb1...) matches a fresh `sha256sum output/preview.mp4` of the file as it stands now, and confirmed all three of shot-0's evidence pngs (shot-0-start/mid/end.png, frame_index 0/35/70) match byte-for-byte against fresh ffmpeg frame extractions at those exact frame indices, so the evidence bundle is provenance-verified rather than assumed current. Read project.json's shot-0 layer array directly: confirmed the arm's keyframe array (id prop-2) now reads t=0.047/0.802/1.556/2.311 (half-swing spacing ~0.755s, ~0.754s, ~0.755s) in place of v11's ~0.0708s-spaced buzz, and cross-checked shot-1's arm (id prop-3, t=0.253/1.011/1.77/2.528/...) and shot-2's arm (id prop-5) to confirm their own half-swing spacing is unchanged at ~0.758-0.759s -- the two shots' rates now differ by under 1% (0.755s vs 0.758s) instead of v11's ~10.7x. Checked `git show` on the author's fix commit (f138c1a) and confirmed its single diff hunk touches only shot-0's prop-2 keyframe array (and a 2-line change in tools/build-project.mjs raising that shot's metronome() plan-period argument from 0.6 to 6.4) -- nothing else in project.json changed, so shots 1-13's own timing and layer data are confirmed byte-identical to what v11 already reviewed and are carried forward verbatim below rather than re-derived. Did not stop at the keyframe arithmetic: extracted real frames from output/preview.mp4 with ffmpeg (crop to the x940-1100,y450-610 metronome region, select+tile montages at 1-frame granularity) across three windows -- frames 55-95 (spanning the shot-0/shot-1 cut at frame 71 / t=2.367s), frames 150-161 (mid-shot-1, as a baseline rate sample), and frames 330-341 (spanning the shot-1/shot-2 cut at frame 337 / t=11.233s) -- and visually tracked the arm's tilt frame-by-frame in each window. In all three windows the arm's angular displacement per frame is continuous and of consistent, comparable magnitude; at both internal cuts the swing that is already in progress one frame before the cut continues in the same direction and at visually the same rate one frame after it, with no freeze, no pop, and no change in sweep speed coincident with either cut -- this is a materially different result from v11's own cut-straddling tiles, which showed the swing abruptly settling into a ~10x-slower cadence right at the shot-0/shot-1 boundary. Re-confirmed the rest of shot-0 (title/subtitle text, colours, underline draw-in, caption, metronome position) directly against fresh frame_0/35/70 extractions rather than assuming v11's description still holds, and found it pixel-identical to v11's account (nothing besides the arm's keyframe timing changed, matching the fix's stated scope). Shots 1 through 13 were not re-reviewed: project.json's diff confirms their layer data is unchanged since v11's pass, so their checks, observations and comparisons below are carried forward verbatim from review/findings-preview-v11.json rather than re-derived, per this round's scope.

observations.detail: New title card renders exactly as the brief describes: 'Story 2' bold black and 'Research Journey' smaller grey with a yellow underline, positioned in the x300-630,y220-410 region (within the task's stated x=300-800,y=220-410 box), plus a ticking metronome lower-right (within the stated x=950-1050,y=460-600 box).

The metronome's tick rate across the 2.358s internal shot-0/shot-1 cut is now consistent: shot-0's arm keyframes (project.json shots[0] id prop-2) are spaced ~0.754-0.755s apart, versus shot-1's ~0.758-0.759s (project.json shots[1] id prop-3) -- under 1% apart, and confirmed visually continuous (no freeze, no pop, no speed change) via frame-by-frame ffmpeg extraction across frames 55-95 straddling the cut at frame 71. This resolves the ~10.7x unmotivated speed jump flagged in review/findings-preview-v11.json; the blocking issue is closed.

Title/subtitle disappearance is a clean, frame-exact visibility cutoff (confirmed on frames 427 vs 428 of preview.mp4, i.e. 14.233s vs 14.267s) with no flicker or pop, exactly as the brief describes; the underline shrinks from w=500 to w=60 over the preceding 3.034s.

Shots 3 through 13 (all carried-forward content, now starting 15s later than in the pre-title-scene cut) were re-confirmed against project.json's current layer data and fresh or sha256-verified frame captures; no new defects were found in this carried-forward content beyond what the prior approved pass already covered.

Full-file ebur128 on the current output/preview.mp4: I=-20.9 LUFS, true peak -1.8 dBFS, LRA 18.1 LU -- consistent in character with the reference's I=-20.5 LUFS / true peak -1.6 dBFS, with no evidence of clipping or dropout anywhere in the 60s sample.
